decision.summary: Two regions stand out: (1) an abrupt multi-sample drop near index 492–494 across all axes, possibly indicating a temporary offset or jump; (2) a gradual ramp-up in E (and supporting N/U) from ~610 to 625, forming a platform-like feature amid otherwise noisy behavior. Both warrant closer inspection for physical or instrumental origin.

regions.observation: Sharp multi-sample drop in N and E components around index 492–494, with U also dropping; followed by a sustained offset (platform-like) through ~498 before partial recovery. The change is abrupt and spans several samples, suggesting a possible transient displacement or measurement shift.

Sustained upward trend in E component from ~610 to 625, accompanied by correlated rise in N and U; appears as a ramp-like platform rather than noise. Preceded by relative stability and followed by continued high-amplitude variability—suggests possible slow slip or instrumental drift onset.
